title: Tučepi Travel Guide: Beaches, Parking & Where to Stay
metaDescription: Plan your trip to Tučepi with our factual guide. Discover the best neighbourhoods, parking tips, pebble beaches, and driving routes from Central Europe.
intro:
Tučepi is a coastal town on the Makarska Riviera, known for having the longest continuous pebble beach in the region. Extending for four kilometres, the beachfront is backed by a pine-shaded promenade and the steep limestone cliffs of the Biokovo mountain range. It appeals primarily to families and couples seeking a resort-style holiday with immediate beach access, straightforward amenities, and a focus on seaside relaxation rather than historic sightseeing.

The town is built mostly below the D8 coastal highway, making the beachfront areas highly walkable and largely separated from transit traffic. Summer brings dense crowds and peak prices, making June and September the optimal months for swimming with fewer visitors. Those arriving by car will find parking at a premium, requiring accommodation with dedicated private spaces.

quickFacts.label: Best months
quickFacts.value: June and September (warm sea, fewer crowds)

areas.name: Kraj (Centre & Marina)
areas.summary: The busy hub of Tučepi around the marina, packed with restaurants, cafes, and excursion boats. It is the most convenient area if you want everything at your doorstep, but it is also the busiest and noisiest in summer.

areas.name: Slatina
areas.parking: Large hotel lots, easier than the centre
areas.summary: Located in the western part of the town, Slatina is defined by large family resorts and the Slatina Sports Centre. The beach here is very wide, shaded by pines, and offers numerous water sports and inflatable playgrounds.

areas.name: Kamena
areas.summary: The easternmost neighbourhood of Tučepi, offering a more relaxed atmosphere away from the main marina crowds. It is closer to the forested trail leading to the naturist Nugal beach.

areas.name: Gornji Tučepi
areas.bestFor: Those who want peace, views, and have a car
areas.summary: The historic upper village situated in the foothills of Mount Biokovo. It features traditional stone houses, olive groves, and panoramic views over the Adriatic, perfect for a quiet stay.

whenToGo: Summer dominates in Tučepi. July and August bring the hottest weather, peak sea temperatures of 25°C to 27°C, the highest prices, and dense crowds along the promenade. June and September offer the best balance of warm water for swimming, more breathing room on the beaches, and slightly lower accommodation rates. From October to April, the town is exceptionally quiet; most seasonal hotels, restaurants, and beach bars board up for the winter, leaving only a handful of essential services open for locals.

faq.question: Is Tučepi worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, it is worth visiting if you want a resort-style holiday with a long, continuous pebble beach and mountain backdrops. It is less suited for those seeking a historic old town, as it is primarily a modern beach destination.

faq.question: How many days do I need in Tučepi?
faq.answer: A stay of 5 to 7 days is standard for a summer beach holiday. This allows enough time to relax by the sea, hike in Biokovo Nature Park, and take a boat trip to the nearby islands of Brač or Hvar.

faq.question: What is the best beach in Tučepi?
faq.answer: The main coastline is essentially one long 4-kilometre pebble beach. Slatina Beach in the west is best for families due to its width and pine shade, while Kamena Beach in the east is quieter.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Tučepi?
faq.answer: You do not need a car if you plan to stay by the beach and use local buses or boats for excursions. A car is highly useful if you are renting a villa in Gornji Tučepi or wish to explore the wider Makarska Riviera independently.

faq.question: Where can I park in Tučepi?
faq.answer: Parking is notoriously tight and expensive in the centre, relying mostly on paid municipal lots along the D8 highway. Always confirm that your accommodation includes a dedicated parking spot before booking.

faq.question: Is Tučepi good for families?
faq.answer: Yes, Tučepi is one of the most family-friendly destinations on the Makarska Riviera. The beaches have shallow clear water, the 4-kilometre promenade is flat and stroller-friendly, and there are numerous playgrounds.
